independent_adjudication.title: Mathspace breach exposed personal data of more than one million users in Australia and New Zealand
independent_adjudication.review_scope: Published v0.9.0 two-class delta only; all other class findings preserved, not re-adjudicated.

delta_decisions.basis: Mathspace’s historical logs establish unauthorised access and download of personal records from its reporting database. This crosses the records’ confidentiality boundary independently of subsequent misuse. Credentials were expressly excluded from the corrected exposed-field list, so this does not support a secret-custody finding.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information is held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: The source episodes identify downloaded school-user personal records within the participating AI-mediated workflow or dependent infrastructure.

condition_tests.literal_condition: An independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary restricts access, acquisition, disclosure or modification of that information for the actor, operation and context.
condition_tests.assessment: The independently evidenced boundary is Mathspace’s restricted reporting-database audience.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Occurrence evidence demonstrates that at least one such information operation crosses that boundary. A successful unauthorised retrieval or modification is sufficient; a theoretical route alone is not.
condition_tests.assessment: The realised operation is identified by the source-local decision: The attacker downloaded personal information from Mathspace’s reporting database. The affected records were restricted school-user information, not public statistics.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information and its independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary are established for an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The identified information and boundary are downloaded school-user personal records, governed by Mathspace’s restricted reporting-database audience.

condition_tests.literal_condition: A concrete access, acquisition, disclosure or modification attempt or operation materially tests that boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The concrete test is: The attacker downloaded personal information from Mathspace’s reporting database. The affected records were restricted school-user information, not public statistics.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Observed response or verification shows that the unauthorised information operation is prevented or that the operation remains within its authorised information boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

condition_tests.literal_condition: The protective conclusion is restricted to the tested information, actor, operation and route; the evidence supports that result rather than only a configured policy or a claimed repair.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The information is deliberately public for the assessed operation and no independent integrity or other access restriction governs that operation. Public readability does not authorise public modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The relevant restriction is Mathspace’s restricted reporting-database audience; this is not an unrestricted public read. Publicly readable packages/posts retain separately evidenced write restrictions where assessed.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The only material property is custody of authentication material. Assess Authentication Material Custody Integrity; separate private content or other protected information can independently engage this class.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The access finding concerns downloaded school-user personal records as protected information or a distinct record modification; any secret-only property is separately assigned to the custody class.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: The observed information operation is validly authorised within the independently established boundary. An approved test does not by itself authorise public release of protected information.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The assessed operation is tested against Mathspace’s restricted reporting-database audience. Technical access, research motivation or permission for another target does not authorise crossing this boundary.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Only a hypothetical vulnerability, exposed endpoint, unverified capability claim or unsuccessful attempt is established, without demonstrated protected-information access, acquisition, disclosure or modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The decision relies on the documented operation or named unresolved occurrence fact, not hypothetical severity: Mathspace’s historical logs establish unauthorised access and download of personal records from its reporting database. This crosses the records’ confidentiality boundary independently of subsequent misuse. Credentials were expressly excluded from the corrected exposed-field list, so this does not support a secret-custody finding.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is solely accuracy, availability, provenance, secondary-purpose permission or audit reconstruction, without an independently engaged information access or integrity boundary.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The independently engaged property is Mathspace’s restricted reporting-database audience; a solely accuracy, availability, provenance or audit result would not suffice.
